dse_runs.notes: Spec: 32 requests per 1us tick, all 32 results back within 0.44us (p99), err <= 2^-12, min LUTs+FFs. Memory: pipelined_m m=4 (data_width=15, n_iter=12, angle_guard=2, rounding=round) won a similar bursty p99 spec (8 requests, p99 0.4us, err 2^-10) with est 813 luts+ffs. Here the burst is 4x larger (32) but the window is similar (0.44us), so m>=4 is likely needed; consider m=4..8, data_width 15-18, n_iter 12-15, angle_guard 1-2, rounding=round. Cost model underestimates LUTs ~19%, FFs ~11%, Fmax ~10% vs yosys+nextpnr-xilinx. unrolled_k never reached a front; iterative too slow for burst draining.

final_text:
Campaign complete — all specs finalized.

**multiaxis_control** (the only spec in the queue): I ran the full 400-evaluation L1 structured DSE (architect refined twice, then stopped), which produced a 23-design Pareto front dominated by pipelined_m m=4 designs — consistent with memory from the bursty_offload campaign. L2 SimPy simulation of the top-5 shortlist confirmed all pass the 0.44us p99 batch constraint (simulated 0.378–0.395us), with the winner unchanged: **pipelined_m, data_width=16, n_iter=14, angle_guard=2, frac_guard=2, rounding=round, m=4** — est. 1137 LUTs+FFs (861 LUTs / 276 FFs), 97.8 MSPS throughput, 2^-12.26 max error, simulated p99 0.378us. The ladder subagent ran L3/L4/L5: no recorded RTL verification or synthesis measurements exist for this design (fresh W=16 exhaustive verification too heavy for a live campaign), so back_annotate returned no_measured_data with no winner-change flag, and reexplore was correctly refused. The spec was finalized on the L2 selection, and a lesson note was stored for future campaigns.
